assertions.text: Table uses value-set syntax (curly braces like {READ, WRITE} or {READ, WRITE, DELETE}) to express rules that hold across multiple actions — rather than one row per role/action combination
assertions.evidence: {READ, WRITE, DELETE} for ADMIN, {READ, WRITE} for USER, {WRITE, DELETE} for GUEST

assertions.text: Table has fewer than 9 data rows (i.e. does not enumerate every role/action combination individually)
assertions.evidence: 5 rows in the table (ADMIN unrestricted, USER read or write, USER no delete, GUEST read only, GUEST no write/delete)

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: void shouldEnforcePermissions(Role role, Action action, boolean allowed) { assertEquals(allowed, canPerform(role, action)); }

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: Scenario | Role | Action | Allowed? — 'Scenario' is the leftmost column with descriptive entries like 'ADMIN unrestricted', 'USER read or write', etc.

assertions.text: No two rows share both the same Role value and the same boolean output — forces value set consolidation
assertions.evidence: ADMIN has one row (true), USER has two rows with different outputs (true and false), GUEST has two rows with different outputs (true and false) — no role+output duplicates

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case
assertions.evidence: Method name 'shouldEnforcePermissions' converts to 'Should Enforce Permissions', which is a clear, descriptive title

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express — such as where permissions are checked in the request lifecycle, or open questions. It is acceptable to omit @Description if the table already conveys all relevant context.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation is present; the table itself conveys all relevant context about role-action-permission mappings

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest is present; no ordering violation

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: No @Description annotation present; condition for passing is satisfied
